description: What examples/output/ keeps, applied by tools/prune_outputs.py and called with --apply at the end of every sweep by spec_checks/run_all.py. Same convention as configs/gate_cache.json: every numeric parameter carries a '<name>_allowed_range' sibling of the form 'low..high', inclusive on both ends. The directory holds every artefact every batch ever produced, which is the right thing while a batch is live and dead weight once its successor has been delivered twice over. 'keep_recent_batches' is how many batch directories keep everything they hold, newest first by the batch number in the directory name; every earlier batch directory keeps only the files matching 'keep_patterns', which is what a delivery report and its run log are and is what a later batch is ever read back for. Four things are never pruned whatever this says: a file git tracks, because the repository is the record and what is committed is the evidence; a file corpus/manifest.json names, because a baseline is an input to the gates rather than a product of them; any path listed in 'protected_paths', which is the evidence intake spec_checks/spec_check_e0.py registers by path and SHA-256 and whose whole point is that it is not tracked and cannot be rebuilt; and any directory that is not a batch directory, which is how the gate cache and the timing records are left to the mechanisms that govern them. Before an evicted batch loses anything, every file of it matching 'archive_patterns' and no larger than 'archive_max_file_kb' is packed into docs/reports/archive/<batch>.zip, which IS tracked: batch b9.2 showed that eviction without archiving is indistinguishable from loss, because the sidecars a later batch turns out to need are exactly the small text files that cost nothing to keep. Anything bigger, and anything outside those patterns, is still removed -- the archive is for the record, not for the intermediate language. 'baseline_archive' turns each frozen baseline checkpoint directory into the archive the readers already resolve, which is the same artefact at about a tenth of the disk. 'protected_paths' also carries a second class of entry, which batch b11.2 added: the working files of a run a later batch has taken as its baseline. The list was written for evidence that is registered by path and digest and cannot be rebuilt, and a baseline run's translation tracking and its stage 09 and stage 11 checkpoints are the same thing under a different name -- they are what a later batch measures against, they cost more than 'archive_max_file_kb' allows and so cannot be archived, and rebuilding them means running the pipeline again, which is exactly the comparison a baseline exists to avoid. Raising the archive ceiling to admit them instead was refused: those files run to hundreds of megabytes and the archive is tracked, so admitting them would put the disk this tool exists to bound into git rather than onto the disk. An entry of this class comes out of the list when the batch that named it as a baseline is delivered and nothing points at it any more. Batch b11.3 widened that second class by one stage: the stage 06 checkpoints of the same baseline run. The class was written for the files a later batch measures against, and b11.3 measures against stage 06 -- it is where the formula annotation is written, so it is the only stage that can say why a composition was annotated at all. Registering it is the same narrowing the class already makes and not a new licence: it adds paths the policy may not remove and removes none. It was done while the batch was still reading those files rather than after, because evidence in use and unprotected is the shape GAP-31 already cost this project eight assertions.
